Impact by State

Impact by State

New Haven is Yale’s home, but in partnership with institutions and scholars and through the work of our graduates, we contribute to and learn from communities nationwide — in every state across America. Yale shows up in your backyard.

By investing in people, as well as programs, conferences, events, initiatives, and collaborations, Yale benefits from the unflagging power and determination of people across the country to drive excellence, opportunity, and innovation. We’re proud to have contributed to centuries of national competitiveness through generative and meaningful partnerships with institutions across the country. Explore your state’s impact by clicking through on the map below.

About our graduates

Our graduates come from and contribute to every state

Yale graduates are positioned to do well and to do good. Our alumni are supported by and contributing to communities in every state, strengthening national security, safeguarding national competitiveness, stimulating our economy, and giving back to their neighbors. Yale graduates become transformational leaders, from U.S. presidents and Supreme Court justices to CEOs, Nobel laureates, and Pulitzer Prize winners. Learn more about Yale’s national impact.

9 in 10

Yale College graduates go on to work or study in the United States (Class of 2024)

87%

of undergraduates graduated debt-free (2020–24)

100%

All 50 states are represented by Yale’s graduate and professional students, who go on to work across the country in academia, for-profit, government, non-profit, and other industries

Exceptional Education 50 states

Yale provides an exceptional education to students from all 50 states and sets them up for success while prioritizing affordability.

  • 95.7% of students (and 95.5% of Pell-eligible students) who entered Yale College in 2018 graduated within six years.
  • 94% of Yale College graduates were employed or in graduate school within six months of graduation (Class of 2024).
  • 54% of undergraduates received financial aid, with an average annual aid package of $75,854 (Class of 2029).
  • 7x more veterans, and 2x more Pell Grant and first-generation college students, were enrolled in Yale’s first-year class, compared to a decade ago.

Equal Opportunity and Nondiscrimination at Yale University: The university is committed to basing judgments concerning the admission, education, and employment of individuals upon their qualifications and abilities and seeks to attract to its faculty, staff, and student body qualified persons from a broad range of backgrounds and perspectives. Additionally, in accordance with this Policy and as delineated by federal and Connecticut law, Yale does not discriminate in admissions, educational programs, or employment against any individual on account of that individual’s sex; sexual orientation; gender identity or expression; pregnancy, childbirth or related conditions; race; color; national or ethnic origin; religion; age; disability; protected veteran status, or other protected classes as set forth in federal and Connecticut law. Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 protects people from sex discrimination in educational programs and activities at institutions that receive federal financial assistance. See Yale’s full Equal Opportunity & Nondiscrimination Statement.
